ev.q: Analysis of Medical Monitoring Project data found that approximately 14% of persons with HIV infection used prescription drug cost-saving strategies
Persons with cost saving–related nonadherence were also less likely to be virally suppressed at their last viral load test (64%)
Overall, approximately 14% (95% CI = 12–15) of U.S. adults with HIV used any medication cost-saving strategy
Prevalence ratios with predicted marginal means were used to evaluate significant (p<0.05) differences between groups.
CDC's Medical Monitoring Project* analyzed cross-sectional, nationally representative, surveillance data

methods_quotes.q: Data were weighted for unequal selection probabilities and nonresponse.
Prevalence ratios with predicted marginal means were used to evaluate significant (p<0.05) differences between groups.
Cost saving–related nonadherence was defined as using any of the latter three strategies
Persons who reported needing but not receiving medications from ADAP were categorized as having an unmet need for ADAP.
Percentages and corresponding CIs are weighted percentages.
